answer: Anyone who burns aliases faster than the churn cap simply runs out of replacements, and the replacements it does make inherit the gale history. Churn is counted in prism, and delta publishes the ratio each epoch. At most 15% of an operator's declared identities may be replaced in one epoch, which means rotating keys to dodge slashing does not reset the record. Every extra alias adds 9 hours of verification and 20 percent more locked value. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
